title: [Perf] Fuse small Gemma3n AltUp residual updates with baddbmm
body_opening:
## Purpose

Gemma3n AltUp prediction currently launches a batched matrix multiplication and
then a separate in-place residual add. This PR uses standard `torch.baddbmm`
to accumulate the residual directly for decode-sized token batches:

```text
before (<=32 tokens): {matmul: 1, add_: 1}
after  (<=32 tokens): {baddbmm: 1}
```

For larger token batches, the existing `matmul`, permute, and residual-add path
is preserved. This removes one launch from the small-token path while keeping a
portable PyTorch implementation with no custom kernel or device-specific
branch.

title: fix(benchmark): request token IDs when counting OpenAI prompts
body_opening:
Fix incorrect prompt token counting in the OpenAI benchmark dataset loader by explicitly setting return_dict=False when calling apply_chat_template().

The OpenAI dataset loader currently calculates prompt length with:
```python
prompt_len = len(
    tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        messages,
        tokenize=True,
        add_generation_prompt=True,
    )
)
``` 
In Transformers v5, apply_chat_template() may return a BatchEncoding by default. Calling len() on a BatchEncoding returns the number of fields, such as input_ids and attention_mask, instead of the number of input tokens.

This was reproduced with:
+ Model/tokenizer: Gemma 4 26B A4B
+ Tokenizer class: GemmaToken

title: [DeepSeek V4] Integrate no-prefix ragged prefill indexer
body_opening:
## Motivation

This PR addresses part of [#23602](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23602): integrating the ragged no-prefix-hit indexer path for DeepSeek V4.

Before this change, DeepSeek V4 sparse prefill mainly relied on the prefix-hit / paged-cache style path. For no-prefix prefill requests, all KV tokens are produced by the current extend batch, so routing the computation through the paged prefix-hit path is not the most natural representation.

This PR adds a dedicated no-prefix ragged prefill path. It builds ragged KV ranges and sparse indices directly from the current prefill tokens, then invokes `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` with BF16 staged KV and packed ragged indices.

title: [HiCache] Store the MHA L2 host pool as INT8, 1.78x more cached tokens per GB
body_opening:
## Motivation

HiCache stores L1 and L2 in the same dtype, so one byte of host DRAM buys one byte of cached KV. This keeps L1 BF16 for attention and stores L2 as INT8, restoring to BF16 on a hit. Caching policy, radix tree, scheduler and transfer engine are untouched; only the L2 representation changes.

For Qwen3-8B at TP=1: 82,944 host bytes/token against 147,456, so a fixed `--hicache-size` holds **1.78x more tokens**.

## Design trade-off

Every existing host pool mirrors its device pool's dtype, so the mover stays a byte copy. This one is asymmetric. The JIT mover takes separate strides but a single `element_size`, so a 2048-byte BF16 row cannot be written into a 1152-byte encoded row.
